passage:
Charu: so you're just not coming to my cousin's wedding? after I told everyone?
Naveen: I said I might not get leave. you're twisting it
Charu: I'm twisting it?? you always do this
Naveen: my jaw's clenched and I'm typing things I'll regret
Naveen: I need a break. going for a walk. I'll text you by 9, promise
Charu: fine
Naveen: 8:50. back. calmer
Naveen: sorry for saying you twisted it. the real problem: I asked for leave and my manager hasn't replied. I'm stressed and took it out on you
Charu: I got loud too. I was embarrassed because I'd already told Masi
Naveen: if the leave doesn't come through, can we call Masi together?
Charu: yes. thank you for coming back to it

qa.q: What time did Naveen come back to the chat?
What was Naveen feeling when writing about a clenched jaw?
qa.a: Naveen was angry and stressed, noticing the clenched jaw and fearing messages that would be regretted.

qa.q: Why wasn't Naveen's break just avoidance?
qa.a: Naveen named a return time, came back calmer, and honestly raised the real problem about the leave instead of dropping it.

qa.q: How might Charu have felt when Naveen wrote "I need a break"?
qa.a: Charu may have felt brushed off at first, replying only "fine", until Naveen came back as promised.

grounding: Someone notices anger in the body, takes a break with a set time to return, and comes back to talk honestly without blame.

passage:
Behind the counter of the family's kirana shop in Nabha, Jyoti found the account book short again. "Tarun, you took money from the drawer without writing it down!"
"It was for Bebe's medicines. What, now I need your permission?"
Jyoti felt her face heat up and her hands start to shake. Words were piling up in her mouth, the kind that wouldn't go back in. "I need a break," she said. "I'm too angry right now. I'll come back at closing time."
She walked to the canal and sat under the neem tree until her breathing slowed.
At closing time she came back with two cups of tea. "I'm not blaming you. I just need to know where the money goes. Can we write every withdrawal in the book, even for medicines?"
Tarun took his cup. "Fair. I should have written it."

qa.q: Where did Jyoti go during the break?
qa.a: Jyoti walked to the canal and sat under the neem tree.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling when her face heated up?
qa.a: Jyoti was angry, with shaking hands and hurtful words piling up.

qa.q: How did Jyoti make sure the break was not avoidance?
qa.a: Jyoti said when she would return, came back at closing time with tea, and raised the money problem without blaming.

qa.q: How might Tarun have felt when Jyoti first accused him?
qa.a: Tarun felt defensive and stung, since he had taken the money for Bebe's medicines.

grounding: Someone notices anger rising, says she needs a break, and returns later to talk about the problem without blame.
